Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 4, verses 53–55:

The Jews are described as having two of the worst traits: stinginess and envy. They withhold what they have been given of blessing, and they wish that others should have blessings instead. So He said: ﴿Or do they have a share of the dominion?﴾ on the basis that *am* (or) is *munqati'a* (disjunctive) [[His saying "on the basis that *am* is disjunctive" means it is explained as *bal* (rather) and the hamza (interrogative particle). (ع)]], and the meaning of the hamza is to deny that they have any share of the dominion. Then He said: ﴿then they would not give the people even a *naqir*﴾. That is, if they had a share of the dominion, then they would not give anyone even a *naqir*, because of their extreme stinginess. The *naqir* is the small pit on the back of a date stone, and it is a figure for a very small amount, like the *fatil* (the thread in a date stone) and the *qitmir* (the membrane on a date stone).

The "dominion" may mean either the dominion of the people of this world, or the dominion of God, as in His saying: ﴿Say: If you possessed the treasuries of the mercy of my Lord, you would surely withhold them for fear of spending﴾. This is a more descriptive way of attributing miserliness to them, and it is better because it matches its counterpart in the Qur'an.

It is also permissible that the hamza in *am* means a denial that they have been given any share of dominion, even though they were owners of wealth, gardens and lofty palaces, as is the condition of kings, and that they do not give anyone anything of what they own.

Ibn Mas'ud read: *fa-idhan la yu'tuwna* (with the verb in the subjunctive), by applying the operative force of *idhan*, which is the *nasb* (accusative) effect, whereas in the common reading it is nullified. It is as if it were said: "So they do not give people a *naqir*, if...".

﴿Or do they envy the people?﴾ That is, do they envy the Messenger of God (ﷺ) and the believers? This is a denial of envy and a declaration that it is ugly. They used to envy them for what God had given them of help, victory, increase in honour, and advancement every day.

﴿Indeed We gave the family of Abraham the Book and the wisdom﴾: this is a reminder to them of what they already know, namely that God gave the Book and wisdom to the family of Abraham, who are the forefathers of Muhammad (ﷺ). It is not strange that God should give him what He gave his forefathers.

It is reported from Ibn Abbas: the dominion in the family of Abraham is the dominion of Joseph, David and Solomon. It was also said: they objected to his having many wives, so it was said to them: how can you object to him having nine, when David had a hundred and Solomon had three hundred free wives and seven hundred concubines?

﴿So among them there is one who believed in it﴾, that is, in what was mentioned concerning the family of Abraham. ﴿And among them there is one who turned away from it﴾, that is, denied it although he knew it to be true. Or: among the Jews there were some who believed in the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and some who denied his prophethood. Or: among the family of Abraham there were some who believed in Abraham, and some who disbelieved, as in His saying: ﴿Among them are those who are guided, and many of them are defiantly disobedient﴾.

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 4, verse 56:

﴿We shall replace them with other skins﴾: that is, We shall exchange them for other than them. If you ask: how is punishment inflicted on other skins, which have not disobeyed, in place of the skins that disobeyed? I answer: the punishment is for the sensitive body as a whole, namely that which disobeyed, not for the skin alone. And on the authority of Fudayl (Fudayl ibn ʿIyad):

It makes the cooked (skin) into something other than cooked.

And on the authority of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): "Their skins are changed every day seven times." [I have not found it. Ibn ʿAdi and al-Tabarani (narrate) from Ibn ʿUmar: a man recited before ʿUmar (﴿Every time their skins are cooked through, We shall replace them with other skins﴾), and Muʿadh said: they are changed every hour a hundred times. ʿUmar said: this is how I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). In its chain is Nafiʿ ibn Yusuf al-Sulami and Abu Hurmuz, who is weak. Ishaq ibn Rahawayh said in his Musnad: Fudayl ibn ʿIyad was asked about this verse, and he informed us from Hisham from al-Hasan who said: their skins are changed seventy thousand times every day.]] And on the authority of al-Hasan: seventy times. They will exchange skins white as parchment, ﴿so that they may taste the punishment﴾.

So that the taste of it may remain for them and not cease, like your saying to the honored one: "May Allah honor you," meaning: may He keep you in your honor and increase you in it. ﴿Mighty﴾: nothing that He wills against the criminals can be prevented from Him. ﴿Wise﴾: He punishes only with justice toward whoever deserves it.

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 4, verses 57–58:

ẓalīlan (ظَلِيلًا) is a qualifier derived from the word ẓill (shade), used to emphasise its meaning, as one says: laylun alīl (a very dark night), and yawmun ayyam (a very long day), and the like. It is that which is fīnān (ظل فينان, dense and spreading), with no gap or break in it, and dā'iman (perpetual), which the sun does not abrogate (lā tansakhuhu al-shams), and sajsajan (وسجسجاً) [[His saying "fīnānan" means long and extended. al-jawb means a tear or a cut. al-sajsaj means moderate. Reported by al-Ṣiḥāḥ. (ʿA)]], neither hot nor cold in it. And that is none other than the shade of Paradise. May God, by His grace, grant us the means to take refuge in that shade. In the reading of ʿAbd Allah: sa-yudkhiluhum (with the yā', "He will admit them"). Inna Allāha yaʾmurukum an tuʾaddū al-amānāt (إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ أَنْ تُؤَدُّوا الْأَمَانَاتِ, "Indeed, God commands you to render the trusts to their owners"): the address is general, to everyone, concerning every trust.

It is said it was revealed concerning ʿUthmān ibn Ṭalḥa ibn ʿAbd al-Dār, who was the keeper (sādin) of the Kaʿba. When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) entered Mecca on the day of the Conquest, ʿUthmān closed the door of the Kaʿba and climbed onto the roof, and refused to hand over the key to him, saying: "Had I known that he was the Messenger of God, I would not have prevented him." ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (may God be pleased with him) twisted his arm, took the key from him, opened the Kaʿba, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) entered and prayed two rak'ahs. When he came out, al-ʿAbbās asked him to give him the key and to combine for him the watering (al-siqāya) and the keeping (al-sidāna). Then the verse was revealed, and he commanded ʿAlī to return the key to ʿUthmān and to apologise to him. ʿUthmān said to ʿAlī: "You coerced and harmed me, and then you came to me gently?" He replied: "God has revealed a Qur'an concerning your matter," and he recited the verse to him. ʿUthmān said: "I bear witness that there is no god but God, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is the Messenger of God." Then Gabriel descended and informed the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that the keeping of the Kaʿba would remain among the descendants of ʿUthmān forever [[Thus al-Thaʿlabi then al-Baghawi mentioned it without a chain of narration. Likewise al-Wāḥidi mentioned it in al-Wasīṭ and al-Asbāb, and he said in it: "As long as this House stands, the key and the keeping are in the descendants of ʿUthmān."]].

It is also said that it is an address to the rulers (al-wulāt) to render the trusts and to judge with justice. It is read al-amānah (in the singular, ﴿الأمانة﴾). ẓalīlan (ظَلِيلًا) is a qualifier derived from the word ẓill (shade), used to emphasise its meaning, as one says: laylun alīl (a very dark night), and yawmun ayyam (a very long day), and the like. It is that which is fīnān (ظل فينان, dense and spreading), with no gap or break in it, and dā'iman (perpetual), which the sun does not abrogate (lā tansakhuhu al-shams), and sajsajan (وسجسجاً) [[His saying "fīnānan" means long and extended. al-jawb means a tear or a cut. al-sajsaj means moderate. Reported by al-Ṣiḥāḥ. (ʿA)]], neither hot nor cold in it. And that is none other than the shade of Paradise. May God, by His grace, grant us the means to take refuge in that shade. In the reading of ʿAbd Allah: sa-yudkhiluhum (with the yā', "He will admit them"). Inna Allāha yaʾmurukum an tuʾaddū al-amānāt (إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَأْمُرُكُمْ أَنْ تُؤَدُّوا الْأَمَانَاتِ, "Indeed, God commands you to render the trusts to their owners"): the address is general, to everyone, concerning every trust.

It is said it was revealed concerning ʿUthmān ibn Ṭalḥa ibn ʿAbd al-Dār, who was the keeper (sādin) of the Kaʿba. When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) entered Mecca on the day of the Conquest, ʿUthmān closed the door of the Kaʿba and climbed onto the roof, and refused to hand over the key to him, saying: "Had I known that he was the Messenger of God, I would not have prevented him." ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib (may God be pleased with him) twisted his arm, took the key from him, opened the Kaʿba, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) entered and prayed two rak'ahs. When he came out, al-ʿAbbās asked him to give him the key and to combine for him the watering (al-siqāya) and the keeping (al-sidāna). Then the verse was revealed, and he commanded ʿAlī to return the key to ʿUthmān and to apologise to him. ʿUthmān said to ʿAlī: "You coerced and harmed me, and then you came to me gently?" He replied: "God has revealed a Qur'an concerning your matter," and he recited the verse to him. ʿUthmān said: "I bear witness that there is no god but God, and I bear witness that Muḥammad is the Messenger of God." Then Gabriel descended and informed the Messenger of God (ﷺ) that the keeping of the Kaʿba would remain among the descendants of ʿUthmān forever [[Thus al-Thaʿlabi then al-Baghawi mentioned it without a chain of narration. Likewise al-Wāḥidi mentioned it in al-Wasīṭ and al-Asbāb, and he said in it: "As long as this House stands, the key and the keeping are in the descendants of ʿUthmān."]].

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 4, verse 59:

When He commanded the rulers to render trusts to their owners and to judge with justice, He commanded the people to obey them and to submit to their judgments. What is meant by "those in authority among you" (ulu al-amr minkum) is the rulers of truth, because the rulers of oppression (umara' al-jawr) are disavowed by Allah and His Messenger, so they are not joined with Allah and His Messenger in the obligation of obedience. Rather, what joins Allah and His Messenger are those rulers who agree with them in preferring justice, choosing the truth, enjoining these two and forbidding their opposites, such as the Rightly-Guided Caliphs (al-Khulafa' al-Rashidun) and those who follow them in goodness. The caliphs used to say: "Obey me as long as I act justly among you; but if I oppose (the truth), then you owe me no obedience." It is related from Abu Hazim that Maslama ibn Abd al-Malik said to him: "Did you not used to be commanded to obey us, in His saying: (and those in authority among you)?" He said: "Has He not removed (that obligation) from you when you oppose the truth, in His saying: (If you dispute about anything, refer it to Allah and the Messenger)?" It is also said: they are the commanders of the expeditionary units (al-sara·ya). And from the Prophet ﷺ: "Whoever obeys me has obeyed Allah, and whoever disobeys me has disobeyed Allah, and whoever obeys my commander has obeyed me, and whoever disobeys my commander has disobeyed me." [Agreed upon from the hadith of Abu Hurayra. Al-Bukhari from the narration of al-A'raj. Muslim from the narration of al-A'raj and Abu Salama, both from him.] It is also said: they are the religious scholars who teach people the religion and enjoin them to what is right and forbid them from what is wrong. (If you dispute about anything) means: if you and those in authority among you differ about some matter of religion, then refer it to Allah and His Messenger, that is: return to the Book and the Sunnah regarding it. And how can obedience to the rulers of oppression be obligatory, when Allah has made the command to obey those in authority conditional in a way that leaves no doubt? He first commanded them to render trusts and to judge with justice, and then commanded them to return to the Book and the Sunnah concerning what is unclear. The rulers of oppression do not render trusts, nor do they judge with justice, nor do they refer anything back to the Book or the Sunnah; they only follow their desires wherever those carry them. So they have stripped themselves of the attributes of those who are "those in authority" in the sight of Allah and His Messenger, and the most fitting name for them is: plundering usurpers. That (thatun) refers to the referral to the Book and the Sunnah: (that is better for you and more suitable) and (better in outcome). It is also said: (better in interpretation) than your own interpretation.

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 4, verses 60–63:

It is narrated that Bishr, a hypocrite (munafiq), had a dispute with a Jew. The Jew invited him to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the hypocrite invited him to Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf. Then they both referred the matter to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he ruled in favour of the Jew, but the hypocrite was not satisfied and said: "Come, let us refer it to Umar ibn al-Khattab." The Jew said to Umar: "The Messenger of Allah ruled for us, but he did not accept his ruling." Umar said to the hypocrite: "Is that so?" He said: "Yes." Umar said: "Wait where you are until I come out to you." He went in, girded on his sword, then came out and struck the hypocrite's neck with it until he was cold (dead). Then he said: "This is how I judge for the one who does not accept the judgment of Allah and His Messenger." So the verse was revealed. Jibril said: "Umar has distinguished between truth and falsehood." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to him: "You are al-Faruq."

[Al-Tha'labi transmitted it through the narration of al-Kalbi from Abu 'Asim from Ibn 'Abbas concerning this verse: it was revealed concerning a man of the hypocrites called Bishr. His chain to al-Kalbi is in the introduction of his book. Al-Wahidi also mentioned it. Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh have, through the narration of Wahb from Ibn Lahi'a from Abu al-Aswad: "Two men disputed before the Prophet (ﷺ), and he ruled between them. The one against whom he ruled said: 'Send us back to Umar.' So they both went to him, and he struck the neck of the one who had said: 'Send us back to Umar.' The other came and informed him, and said: 'I did not think Umar would dare to kill a believer.' So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿But no, by your Lord, they will not believe﴾ — the verse — and so his blood was declared forfeit."]

"Al-Taghut" refers to Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf. Allah called him "taghut" because of his extreme transgression (tughyan) and his enmity towards the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). Or it is by way of comparison with the devil, and naming him by his name. Or, the choice of referring to someone other than the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) over referring to him is considered a referral to the devil, as evidenced by His saying: ﴿And they had been commanded to reject it, while Satan intends to lead them far astray.﴾

It is recited as "bima anzala ... wa-ma anzala" (with what was revealed ... and what was revealed) in the active voice (lit. "built for the subject"). 'Abbas ibn al-Fadl recited "an yakfuru biha" (that they reject it, feminine pronoun), taking "taghut" to be plural in meaning, like His saying: ﴿their protectors are the taghut, who bring them out﴾. Al-Hasan recited "ta'alaw" (come) with a damma on the lam, as the lam was elided from "ta'alayta" for lightness, just as they say "ma baliyta bihi balah" (I did not care for it at all), whose origin is "balyah," like "afiyah." Al-Kisa'i said of "ayah" (sign) that its origin is "ayyah," with the lam elided; when it was elided, the waw of the plural came after the lam in "ta'al," so it was given a damma, making "ta'alaw," like "taqaddamu" (advance). From this is the saying of the people of Makkah: "Ta'ala," with a kasra on the lam, to a woman.

In the verse of al-Hamdani:

"Ta'ali uqasimka al-humuma ta'ali" (Come, let me share with you my worries, come)

[The poet says, when a dove has wailed near me: "O my neighbour, has your state become like my state?

By the sanctity of love, you have not tasted the visitation of separation, nor have worries ever occurred to your mind.

O my neighbour, fate has not been fair between us; come, let me share with you my worries, come.

Come, you will see a soul weakened within me, wandering in a body that is tormented by my mind.

Does the captive laugh while the free one weeps, and does the grieving one fall silent while the consoled one laments?

I had more right than you to tears and weeping, but my tears in hardship are precious."

It is attributed to al-Hamdani with a ha'; some narrate it with a ha' (ḥ), and he was a captive. "Bāt" means: your state became like my state in narrowness and grief. The question is one of denial. It is narrated instead: "Hal ta'lamina bihali" (Do you know my state?), and the attribution of knowledge to her is because she is treated as rational, as in his address to her. He said "by the sanctity of love" as one says "ma'adhallah" (by Allah's protection), because of the greatness of love in his sight; it is a verbal noun standing in for its verb, meaning: I seek refuge in love, from the claim that you are like me. "Ma dhaqt" (you have not tasted), O dove, "tarigat" (visitation) of separation, comparing it to a disliked food; tasting is imaginative. "Wa ma khatarat al-humum bi-bal" (nor have worries occurred to a mind of yours): i.e., to a heart of yours. "Aya" is a particle of address. "Jaratā" originally was "jaratī," and the ya' was changed to alif to raise the voice.

The repetition of the address carries the sense of lament. Claiming that she is dull-witted after treating her as rational is far-fetched. "Ma ansafa al-dahr bayna" (fate has not been fair between us), since it released you and captured you, and saddened me. In "ta'ali" — the imperative for a feminine addressee — and in "ta'aliya" for the dual, and in "ta'alaw" for the masculine plural, the lam is pronounced with a fatha, its original vowel, because it is the verbal root's 'ayn, and the pronoun follows its presumed lam. The people of Makkah vowel the first with a kasra for harmony with the ya', and the second with a damma for harmony with the waw, treating it as the lam of the verb. From this is his saying "uqasimka al-humum" (let me share with you my worries): half for me and the other half for you. If it is said that the one who composed this poem was a later (muwallad) poet, so his words cannot be cited as evidence, I answer: its citation falls under exception, not under substitution.

Al-Zamakhshari's view is that "hat," with a kasra, means "hand me," and "ta'ala," always with a fatha in the well-known dialect, means "come to me." Both are names of verbs (ism fi'l), not imperative verbs, perhaps because they are not inflected in these two meanings. More peculiar than this is what al-Suyuti transmitted from some people: that the particles of address are verbal nouns that have become attached to the first-person pronoun, meaning "I call."

His saying "tara" (you see) with a fatha on the ra' according to the first dialect, and with a kasra according to the second. The repetition of the command is like the repetition of the address. The meaning of "the weakness of the soul" is the incapacity of its senses to perceive. "Tuaddadu" (wanders) originally was "tataraddadu" (wanders about); "bali" (my mind) means emaciated. His saying "ayadhak" (does he laugh?) is an interrogative of wonder with respect to the first line, and of reproach with respect to the second, and likewise the second hemistich. It may be that it is of wonder throughout, or of reproach throughout, which is the furthest reading. By "the captive" and "the grieving one" he means himself; by "the free one" and "the consoled one" he means the dove. It is possible that he intended the general sense, and that both enter into it first. "Al-ma'sur" means the imprisoned, and its "huzn" (grief) is the Quraysh dialect; "ahzanah" is the Tamim dialect; "mahzun" comes from the first. "Al-nadbah" is raising the voice in weeping, and what is meant is the earlier wailing. "Al-sali" is the patient one and the one with few worries. "Al-dam'" is the water of the eye and its flowing from it, and the second meaning is what is intended. It is narrated: "bil-dam'i muqlah" (with tears, an eye), where "muqlah" is a specification (tamyiz), and the original is: "laqad kanat muqlatī awla min muqlatika bil-dam'" (my eye had more right than your eye to tears). "Ghali" means elevated, and unassailable against the gloating of the mockers.]

The correct reading is with a fatha on the lam: ﴿fa-kayfa yakūnu ḥāluhum wa-kayfa yaṣna'ūn?﴾ (How will it be with them, and how will they act?). This means they will be incapable at that time, neither issuing a command nor carrying one out. ﴿When a calamity strikes them because of what their hands have sent forth﴾ — namely, their referring to other than you and their accusing you of unfairness in judgment — ﴿then they come to you﴾ — when they are afflicted — ﴿swearing by Allah: "We intended nothing but good and reconciliation"﴾ — meaning, not evil, and bringing about agreement between the two adversaries; we did not intend opposition to you, nor to be displeased with your judgment; so relieve us through your supplication. This is a threat against them for their deed, and that they will regret it when regret will not benefit them, and their excuse will not avail them when the might of Allah descends.

It was also said: the hypocrite's supporters came seeking vengeance for his blood, which Allah had declared forfeit, and they said: "We did not intend by referring to Umar except that he should treat our companion well with a just judgment and bring about agreement between him and his opponent, and it did not occur to us that he would rule in his favour as he did."

﴿So turn away from them﴾ — do not punish them, for there is a benefit in keeping them alive — ﴿and do not add to what they are upon, beyond restraining them with admonition and advice﴾, ﴿and speak to them, concerning themselves, a far-reaching word﴾, which penetrates deeply with admonition by way of gentleness and warning.

If you ask: to what does His saying ﴿concerning themselves﴾ relate?

[Al-Zamakhshari said: "If you ask: to what does His saying 'concerning themselves' relate...?" Ahmad (Ibn al-Munayyir) said: each of these interpretations has a witness that supports its correctness. As for the first, its gist is a command to threaten them in a manner that reaches the core of their hearts, and the context of the threat in His saying ﴿How then, when a calamity strikes them because of what their hands have sent forth, and then they come to you...﴾ supports it, for He informs them of what will happen to them by way of threat. As for the second, the context supports it with His saying ﴿Those are the ones whose hearts Allah knows﴾, meaning what their hearts conceal of wickedness, deceit and tricks. Then He commands him to admonish them and to turn away from their crimes, so that punishing them for them would not prevent him from advising and admonishing them; then His saying ﴿and speak to them, concerning themselves, a far-reaching word﴾ comes as an explanation of the admonition, and of the most important thing to admonish them about: their souls, which Allah knows what they harbour of blameworthy things. On this view, the meaning is the admonition and what relates to it. As for the third, the conduct of the Prophet (ﷺ) supports it, in concealing the hostility of the hypocrites, overlooking their open expression and covering them, to the point that Hudhayfah (may Allah be pleased with him) was counted as his confidant (ﷺ), because he singled him out with knowledge of their persons, and they named themselves to him; and reports on this meaning are numerous.]

I answer: it relates to His saying ﴿a far-reaching word﴾. That is: say to them a far-reaching word concerning themselves, one that has an effect on their hearts, causing them great distress and making them sense fear — namely, a threat of killing and eradication if hypocrisy appears among them and raises its horn. And inform them that what is in their souls of corruption and hypocrisy is known to Allah, and that there is no difference between you and the polytheists; this truce is only because you show faith and conceal unbelief and hide it, and if you do what would expose your covering, nothing will remain but the sword.

Or it relates to His saying ﴿say to them﴾: that is, say to them, concerning their wicked souls and their hearts folded upon hypocrisy, a far-reaching word; and that Allah knows what is in your hearts, nothing is hidden from Him, so your concealing will avail you nothing. Therefore, set your souls right, purify your hearts, and cure them of the sickness of hypocrisy; otherwise Allah will bring upon you what He brought upon those who openly associated others with Him, and worse than that and more severe.

Or: say to them concerning themselves — privately with them, with no one else present, speaking to them confidentially with advice, because it is more effective in secret and penetrates more deeply when sincere — a far-reaching word that reaches them and has an effect upon them.

Or: say to them concerning themselves — privately with them, with no one else present, speaking to them confidentially with advice, because it is more effective in secret and penetrates more deeply when sincere — a far-reaching word that reaches them and has an effect upon them.

﴿وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا مِنْ رَسُولٍ إِلَّا لِيُطَاعَ بِإِذْنِ اللَّهِ﴾ وما أرسلنا رسولا قط إلا ليطاع بسبب إذن الله في طاعته، وبأنه أمر المبعوث إليهم بأن يطيعوه ويتبعوه، لأنه مؤدٍّ عن الله، فطاعته طاعة الله ومعصيته معصية الله. ﴿مَنْ يُطِعِ الرَّسُولَ فَقَدْ أَطَاعَ اللَّهَ﴾. ويجوز أن يراد بـ(بإذن الله) تيسير الله وتوفيقه في طاعته.

﴿وَلَوْ أَنَّهُمْ إِذْ ظَلَمُوا أَنْفُسَهُمْ﴾ بالتحاكم إلى الطاغوت ﴿جَاؤُكَ﴾ تائبين من النفاق، متنصلين مما ارتكبوا، ﴿فَاسْتَغْفَرُوا اللَّهَ﴾ من ذلك بالإخلاص، وبالغوا في الاعتذار إليك من إيذائك بردّ قضائك، حتى انتصبت شفيعا لهم إلى الله ومستغفرا ﴿لَوَجَدُوا اللَّهَ تَوَّابًا﴾ أي لعلموه توابا، أي لتاب عليهم. ولم يقل: «واستغفرت لهم»، بل عدل عنه [[قال محمود: وإنما لم يقل «واستغفرت لهم» لأنه عدل به... الخ» قال أحمد: وفي هذا النوع من الالتفات خصوصية، وهي اشتماله على ذكر صفة مناسبة لما أضيف إليه، وذلك زائد على الالتفات بذكر الأعلام الجامدة، والله الموفق.]] إلى طريقة الالتفات، تفخيما لشأن رسول الله (ﷺ) وتعظيما لاستغفاره، وتنبيها على أن شفاعة من اسمه الرسول من الله بمكان.

﴿فَلَا وَرَبِّكَ﴾ معناه: فو ربك. [[قال محمود: «معناه فو ربك، و«لا» مزيدة لتأكيد... الخ» قال أحمد: يشير إلى أن (لا) لما زيدت مع القسم وإن لم يكن المقسم به، دل ذلك على أنها إنما تدخل فيه لتأكيد القسم، فإذا دخلت حيث يكون المقسم عليه نفيا، تعين جعلها لتأكيد القسم، طردا للباب. والظاهر عندي والله أعلم: أنها هنا لتوطئة النفي المقسم عليه، والزمخشري لم يذكر مانعا من ذلك، وحاصل ما ذكره مجيئها لغير هذا المعنى في الإثبات، وذلك لا يأبى مجيئها في النفي على الوجه الآخر من التوطئة، على أن في دخولها على القسم المثبت نظرا، وذلك أنها لم ترد في الكتاب العزيز إلا مع القسم، حيث يكون بالفعل، مثل ﴿لَا أُقْسِمُ بِهَذَا الْبَلَدِ﴾، ﴿لَا أُقْسِمُ بِيَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ﴾، ﴿فَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِالْخُنَّسِ﴾، ﴿فَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِمَوَاقِعِ النُّجُومِ﴾، ﴿فَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِمَا تُبْصِرُونَ وَمَا لَا تُبْصِرُونَ﴾، ولم تدخل أيضا إلا على القسم بغير الله تعالى، ولذلك سر يأبى كونها في آية النساء لتأكيد القسم. ويعين كونها للتوطئة، وذلك أن المراد بها في جميع الآيات التي عددناها تأكيد تعظيم المقسم به، إذ لا يقسم بالشيء إلا إعظاما له، فكأنه بدخولها يقول: إن إعظامي لهذه الأشياء بالقسم بها كلا إعظام، يعني أنها تستوجب من التعظيم فوق ذلك، وهذا التأكيد إنما يؤتى به رفعا لتوهم كون هذه الأشياء غير مستحقة للتعظيم وللإقسام بها، فيزاح هذا الوهم بالتأكيد في إبراز فعل القسم مؤكدا بالنفي المذكور. وقد قرر الزمخشري هذا المعنى في دخول (لا) عند قوله: ﴿لَا أُقْسِمُ بِيَوْمِ الْقِيَامَةِ﴾ على وجه مجمل، هذا بسطه وإيضاحه، فإذا بين ذلك، فهذا الوهم الذي يراد إزاحته في القسم بغير الله مندفع في الأقسام بالله، فلا يحتاج إلى دخول (لا) مؤكدة للقسم، فيتعين حملها على الموطئة، ولا تكاد تجدها في غير الكتاب العزيز داخلة على قسم مثبت. وأما دخولها في القسم وجوابه نفي فكثير مثل:

فلا وأبيك ابنة العامري ... لا يدعى القوم أني أفر

وكقوله:

ألا نادت أمامة باحتمال ... لتحزنني فلا بك ما أبالي

وقوله:

رأى برقا فأوضع فوق بكر ... فلا بك ما أسال ولا أقاما

وقوله:

فخالف فلا والله تهبط تلعة ... من الأرض إلا أنت للذل عارف

وهو أكثر من أن يحصى، فتأمل هذا الفصل فإنه حقيق بالتأمل.]] كقوله تعالى: ﴿فَوَرَبِّكَ لَنَسْأَلَنَّهُمْ﴾، و«لا» مزيدة لتأكيد معنى القسم، كما زيدت في ﴿لِئَلَّا يَعْلَمَ﴾ لتأكيد وجود العلم. ﴿لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ جواب القسم.

فإن قلت: هلا زعمت أنها زيدت لتظاهر (فَلَا) في ﴿لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾؟ قلت: يأبى ذلك استواء النفي والإثبات فيه، وذلك قوله: ﴿فَلَا أُقْسِمُ بِمَا تُبْصِرُونَ وَمَا لَا تُبْصِرُونَ * إِنَّهُ لَقَوْلُ رَسُولٍ كَرِيمٍ﴾.

﴿فِيمَا شَجَرَ بَيْنَهُمْ﴾ فيما اختلف بينهم واختلط، ومنه الشجر لتداخل أغصانه. ﴿حَرَجًا﴾ ضيقا، أي لا تضيق صدورهم من حكمك. وقيل: شكا، لأن الشاك في ضيق من أمره حتى يلوح له اليقين. ﴿وَيُسَلِّمُوا﴾ وينقادوا ويذعنوا لما تأتي به من قضائك، لا يعارضوه بشيء، من قولك: سلم الأمر لله وأسلم له. وحقيقة (سلم نفسه وأسلمها) إذا جعلها سالمة له خالصة. ﴿تَسْلِيمًا﴾ تأكيد للفعل بمنزلة تكريره، كأنه قيل: وينقادوا لحكمه انقيادا لا شبهة فيه، بظاهرهم وباطنهم.

ابن أبي حاتم: حدثنا عمرو بن عثمان، حدثنا سعيد بن عبد العزيز، عن الزهري، عن سعيد بن المسيب - قوله تعالى: ﴿فَلَا وَرَبِّكَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ - الآية، قال: نزلت في الزبير بن العوام وحاطب بن أبي بلتعة، اختصما في ماء، فقضى النبي (ﷺ) أن يسقي الأعلى ثم الأسفل. وأصله في الصحيحين أتم من هذا من غير تسمية حاطب، أخرجاه من طريق الزهري عن عروة قال: «اختصم الزبير ورجل من الأنصار في شراج الحرة، فقال النبي (ﷺ): اسق يا زبير ثم أرسل الماء إلى جارك. فقال الأنصاري: يا رسول الله، إن كان ابن عمتك؟ فتلون وجهه (ﷺ)، ثم قال: اسق يا زبير ثم احبس الماء حتى يرجع إلى الجدر، ثم أرسل الماء إلى جارك». واستوعب الزبير حقه في صريح الحكم. قال الزبير: فما أحسب هذه الآيات إلا نزلت في ذلك: ﴿فَلَا وَرَبِّكَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ الآية. وروي أنهما لما خرجا مرا على المقداد، فقال: قاتل الله هؤلاء، يشهدون أنه رسول الله (ﷺ) ثم يتهمونه على قضاء يقضي بينهم، وايم الله لقد أذنبنا مرة في حياة موسى عليه السلام، فدعانا إلى التوبة منه وقال: اقتلوا أنفسكم، ففعلنا، فبلغ قتلانا سبعين ألفا في طاعة ربنا، حتى رضي عنا. فقال ثابت بن قيس بن شماس: أما والله إن الله يعلم مني الصدق، لو أمرني أن أقتل نفسي لقتلتها» ذكره الثعلبي في تفسيره بغير سند عن الصالحي، وإسناده إليه أول الكتاب.]] فغضب حاطب وقال: لأن كان ابن عمتك؟ فتغير وجه رسول الله (ﷺ)، ثم قال: «اسق يا زبير ثم احبس الماء حتى يرجع إلى الجدر واستوف حقك، ثم أرسله إلى جارك». كان قد أشار على الزبير برأي فيه السعة له ولخصمه، فلما أحفظ رسول الله (ﷺ) استوعب للزبير حقه في صريح الحكم. ثم خرجا فمرا على المقداد، فقال: لمن كان القضاء؟ فقال الأنصاري: قضى لابن عمته، ولوى شدقه. ففطن يهودي كان مع المقداد فقال: قاتل الله هؤلاء، يشهدون أنه رسول الله ثم يتهمونه في قضاء يقضي بينهم، وايم الله، لقد أذنبنا ذنبا مرة في حياة موسى، فدعانا إلى التوبة منه وقال: اقتلوا أنفسكم، ففعلنا، فبلغ قتلانا سبعين ألفا في طاعة ربنا حتى رضي عنا. فقال ثابت بن قيس بن شماس: أما والله إن الله ليعلم مني الصدق، لو أمرني محمد أن أقتل نفسي لقتلتها. وروي أنه قال ذلك ثابت وابن مسعود وعمار بن ياسر، فقال رسول الله (ﷺ): «والذي نفسي بيده إن من أمتي رجالا الإيمان أثبت في قلوبهم من الجبال الرواسي» [[لم أجده هكذا، وإنما ذكره الثعلبي عن الحسن ومقاتل قالا: لما نزلت هذه الآية قال عمر وعمار وابن مسعود: «والله لو أمرنا الله لفعلنا، والحمد لله الذي عافانا»، فبلغ النبي (ﷺ) ذلك فقال - فذكره.]]. وروي عن عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه أنه قال: والله لو أمرنا ربنا لفعلنا، والحمد لله الذي لم يفعل بنا ذلك. فنزلت الآية في شأن حاطب، ونزلت في شأن هؤلاء.

قيل: نزلت في شأن المنافق واليهودي. وقيل: في شأن الزبير وحاطب بن أبي بلتعة، وذلك أنهما اختصما إلى رسول الله (ﷺ) في شراج من الحرة كانا يسقيان بها النخل، فقال: «اسق يا زبير ثم أرسل الماء إلى جارك» [[قال ابن أبي حاتم: حدثنا عمرو بن عثمان، حدثنا سعيد بن عبد العزيز، عن الزهري، عن سعيد بن المسيب - قوله تعالى: ﴿فَلَا وَرَبِّكَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ - الآية، قال: نزلت في الزبير بن العوام وحاطب بن أبي بلتعة، اختصما في ماء، فقضى النبي (ﷺ) أن يسقي الأعلى ثم الأسفل. وأصله في الصحيحين أتم من هذا من غير تسمية حاطب، أخرجاه من طريق الزهري عن عروة قال: «اختصم الزبير ورجل من الأنصار في شراج الحرة، فقال النبي (ﷺ): اسق يا زبير ثم أرسل الماء إلى جارك. فقال الأنصاري: يا رسول الله، إن كان ابن عمتك؟ فتلون وجهه (ﷺ)، ثم قال: اسق يا زبير ثم احبس الماء حتى يرجع إلى الجدر، ثم أرسل الماء إلى جارك». واستوعب الزبير حقه في صريح الحكم. قال الزبير: فما أحسب هذه الآيات إلا نزلت في ذلك: ﴿فَلَا وَرَبِّكَ لَا يُؤْمِنُونَ﴾ الآية. وروي أنهما لما خرجا مرا على المقداد، فقال: قاتل الله هؤلاء، يشهدون أنه رسول الله (ﷺ) ثم يتهمونه على قضاء يقضي بينهم، وايم الله لقد أذنبنا مرة في حياة موسى عليه السلام، فدعانا إلى التوبة منه وقال: اقتلوا أنفسكم، ففعلنا، فبلغ قتلانا سبعين ألفا في طاعة ربنا، حتى رضي عنا. فقال ثابت بن قيس بن شماس: أما والله إن الله يعلم مني الصدق، لو أمرني أن أقتل نفسي لقتلتها» ذكره الثعلبي في تفسيره بغير سند عن الصالحي، وإسناده إليه أول الكتاب.]] فغضب حاطب وقال: لأن كان ابن عمتك؟ فتغير وجه رسول الله (ﷺ)، ثم قال: «اسق يا زبير ثم احبس الماء حتى يرجع إلى الجدر واستوف حقك، ثم أرسله إلى جارك». كان قد أشار على الزبير برأي فيه السعة له ولخصمه، فلما أحفظ رسول الله (ﷺ) استوعب للزبير حقه في صريح الحكم. ثم خرجا أنه قال: والله لو أمرنا ربنا لفعلنا، والحمد لله الذي لم يفعل بنا ذلك. فنزلت الآية في شأن حاطب، ونزلت في شأن هؤلاء.

Surah al-Nisa' 4:66–68

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf):

﴿And if We had decreed for them, "Kill yourselves" or "Leave your homes," they would not have done it, except a few of them.﴾ That is: if We had obligated them as We obligated the Children of Israel to kill themselves, or to leave their homes, when they were commanded to repent of worshipping the calf. ﴿They would not have done it, except a few of them.﴾ This is a severe rebuke. The nominative (illa qalilun) is in apposition (badal) to the waw in (fa'alu-hu) [the verb's subject pronoun]. It is also read as ﴿illa qalilan﴾ with the accusative, on the basis of the original exception (istithna' asl), or as "except a few acts" (illa fi'lan qaliIan).

﴿And if they had done what they were admonished to do, following the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), obeying him, and submitting to what he sees and rules, for he is the truthful, the one who is believed, who does not speak from desire,﴾ ﴿it would have been better for them﴾ in their present life and in their final outcome, ﴿and stronger in making them firm﴾ in their faith, and further from wavering in it.

﴿And then⁠—﴾ (wa-idhan) is an answer to an implied question, as if it were said: "What would they also have as a result of being made firm?" So it is said:

﴿And then, if they had remained steadfast, We would surely have given them﴾ because idhan is both an answer and a condition, ﴿from Us, a great reward.﴾ This is like His saying: ﴿and He gives from Himself a great reward﴾, in that the intended meaning is a bounty bestowed from Him, and calling it a reward (ajr) is because it follows from the reward and does not hold except by their steadfastness. ﴿And We would surely have guided them﴾, meaning: We would have shown kindness to them and granted them success to increase in goodness.

Al-Siddiqun: the most excellent Companions of the Prophets, those who came first in affirming them, such as Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, and who were truthful in their words and deeds. This is an encouragement for the believers to obedience, since they are promised the company of the nearest of Allah's servants to Him and the highest in rank with Him. "And how excellent those companions are" (wa hasuna ulaika rafiqa) contains the meaning of wonder, as if it were said: "How excellent are those companions!" Because it is independent, it carries the meaning of wonder. It was read as "wa hasuna" with a sukun on the sin. The one expressing wonder says: "Hasun al-wajh wajhuka!" and "Hasnul-wajhi wajhuka!" with fatha and damma, along with the sukun. The word rafiq (companion), like siddiq and khalit, is the same for the singular and the plural, and it may also be singular, through which the genus is specified in the chapter of tamyiz (specification).

It is narrated that Thawban, the freedman of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, had a very strong love for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and little patience in being apart from him. One day he came to him, his face changed, his body emaciated, and sorrow was visible on his face. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ asked him about his condition, and he said: "O Messenger of Allah, I have no ailment, except that when I do not see you, I long for you and feel a severe loneliness until I meet you. Then I remembered the Hereafter and feared that I would not see you there, because I know that you will be raised with the Prophets, and if I enter Paradise, I would be in a station below yours, and if I do not enter, then that is the time when I will never see you." Then this was revealed, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "By He in whose hand is my soul, no servant truly believes until I am dearer to him than his own self, his parents, his family, his children, and all people." [[Al-Tha'labi mentioned it without a chain, and al-Wahidi transmitted it in al-Asbab from al-Kalbi, but he did not say at its end, "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'By He in whose hand is my soul...' etc." This was related from a group of the Companions. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: Khalaf ibn Khalifa narrated to us from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib from al-Sha'bi who said: "A man from the Ansar came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said to him: 'You are dearer to me than my own self, my children, my family and my wealth. Were it not that I come to you and see you, I would surely (die)'—meaning, I would die—and the Ansari wept. The Prophet ﷺ said to him: 'What makes you weep?' He said: 'I remembered that you will die, and you will be with the Prophets, peace be upon them, and if we enter Paradise, we will be below you.' So Allah revealed to His Messenger ﷺ: '(And whoever obeys Allah...)'—the verse—and he said to him: 'Rejoice.'" Al-Bayhaqi also narrated it through him in Shu'ab al-Iman; al-Tabarani connected it, and Ibn Mardawayh (narrated it) from him. Through the route of Khalid ibn 'Abd al-Rahman from 'Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib from al-Sha'bi from Ibn 'Abbas, something similar. Al-Tabari narrated through the route of Ya'qub al-Qummi from Ja'far ibn Abi al-Mughira from Sa'id ibn Jubayr something similar, as a mursal report. Al-Tabarani in al-Saghir and al-Wahidi narrated it as connected through the route of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Imran al-'Abidi from Fudayl ibn 'Iyad from Mansur ibn Ibrahim from al-Aswad from 'A'isha, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "A man came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, by Allah, you are truly dearer to me than my own self'—the hadith, similar in content. Al-Wahidi also narrated it through another route from Masruq, who said: 'The Companions of Muhammad ﷺ said'—and he mentioned it briefly. And through the route of Rawh from Qatada similarly, as a mursal report.]] This was related from a group of the Companions.

"That" (dhalika) is the subject, "the bounty" (al-fadl) is its attribute, and "from Allah" (min Allah) is the predicate. It is also permissible that "that" is the subject and "the bounty from Allah" is its predicate. The meaning: what the obedient are given of reward [[Mahmud said: "The meaning is that what the obedient are given of reward..." etc. Ahmad says: The creed of the People of the Sunna is that the obedient one does not deserve anything from Allah by his obedience, and whatever he is rewarded with, such as entry into Paradise and salvation from the Fire, is a bounty from Allah, not an established entitlement. They affirm this verse in its hope. As for the Qadariyya, they claim that the obedient one merits from Allah the reward for obedience, and that the reward corresponding to his obedience is a due wage, like the payment for work among people, not a bounty; the bounty is only what the servant is given beyond his due of various kinds of reward and honours. When this verse came, stating explicitly that the whole of what the servants of Allah attain is a bounty from Allah, al-Zamakhshari was compelled to reinterpret it in line with his creed. So he made the bounty referred to the increase that follows the reward, meaning the due portion. Then he extended the interpretation and mentioned another aspect: that what is referred to is the distinctive qualities of these obedient ones in their obedience and their distinction through their deeds, and he took the meaning of it being a bounty from Allah to be that He granted them success in acquiring it and enabled them to do so and nothing more; meaning that their production of it is by their own power. This is from the first class of such interpretation. The truth is that everything is also a bounty from Allah in every respect, because our creed, we the people of the Sunna, is that the acts of obedience and deeds by which these elect are distinguished are the creation and action of Allah, Exalted is He, that their power has no effect on their deeds, but rather Allah, Mighty and Majestic, creates the acts of obedience through their hands and rewards them for them. So obedience is from His bounty, and its reward is from His bounty; to Him belongs the bounty in every state, and the favour in the beginning and the end. And the saying of the master of mankind on this is sufficient proof and example: he, upon whom be the best of prayers and peace, said: "None of you will enter Paradise by his deeds, but by Allah's bounty and mercy." It was said: "Not even you, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Not even I, unless Allah covers me with His bounty and mercy." Say: "By Allah's bounty and His mercy, let them rejoice in that." O Allah, seal our lives with following the Sunna, and admit us by Your pure bounty into Paradise.]] the great reward and the company of those upon whom Allah has bestowed favour, because He has graciously given it to them in addition to their reward. "And Allah suffices as Knower" (wa kafa billahi 'aliman): knowing the recompense of those who obey Him. Or it means: the excellence of those upon whom favour is bestowed and their distinction is from Allah, because they acquired it through His enablement and granting of success; and Allah suffices as Knower of His servants, so He grants them success according to their conditions.

Take your precaution (al-hadhar), and then go forth in groups (thubat), or go forth all together (jamee'an).

Al-hadhar and al-hadhar carry the same meaning, like al-ithr and al-athr. It is said: akhadha hadharahu, when he became alert and guarded himself against what he feared. It is as if he made caution the instrument by which he protects himself and safeguards his life. The meaning is: be wary and guard yourselves against the enemy, and do not allow them access to yourselves. Then go forth (fanfiru) when you march out to the enemy, either in separate detachments, one unit after another (sariyya ba'da sariyya), or all together (jami'an), that is, gathered as a single body (kawkaba wahida). And do not falter and thus throw yourselves into destruction (al-tahlukah). It is also recited fanfuru with a dammah on the fa'.

Al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf), commentary on Surah an-Nisa' 4:72–73:

The lam in (لَمَنْ) is a lam of initiation (lam al-ibtida'), with the same function as in His words (إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَغَفُورٌ). The lam in لَيُبَطِّئَنَّ is the response (jawab) of an omitted oath, its underlying sense being: "And indeed among you is one who swears by Allah that he will surely lag behind." The oath and its response form the relative clause (silah) of "man," and the pronoun referring back from it to "man" is the one concealed within لَيُبَطِّئَنَّ. The address is to the army of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and those who lag behind among them are the hypocrites, because they used to go on raids with them only out of hypocrisy.

The meaning of لَيُبَطِّئَنَّ is: they will surely be sluggish and stay behind from jihad and hold back. Batra' (بطأ) is used in the sense of abta'a (أبطأ), as 'atama (عتم) is used in the sense of a'tama (أعتم), meaning he delayed when he was late. (Note: In al-Sihah, "al-'atm" is defined as "al-ibta'" (delay). — Editor's note.) It is also read as لَيُبَطِّئَنَّ with the lightened form. It is said: bata'a 'ala fulan and abta'a 'alayya and buti'a (بطؤ) in the sense of "thaqula" (to be heavy/slow). It is said: "ma bata'a bika" (what kept you back?), which takes the preposition bi. It is also possible that it is a causative form derived from buti'a, as "thaqula" becomes "thaqqala," so that it means: he will cause others to lag behind, and he will hinder them from the raid. This was the habit of the hypocrite Abd Allah ibn Ubayy, and he is the one who discouraged people on the day of Uhud. (Quoting Mahmud, the author, in this regard: "By the calamity is meant killing or defeat..."). Ahmad (Ibn al-Munayyir) says: In this reading there is a rare subtlety, namely the return to the wording of "man" after returning to its meaning. Some have denied its existence in the Mighty Book, because it entails ambiguity after clarity, which contradicts the principles of eloquence, since returning to its wording does not express its meaning clearly; rather, its reference to the meaning is vague and obscure, so its occurrence after clarification is difficult. Others have affirmed it and counted two places, and this verse in this reading is a third. A clear explanation will follow, Allah willing.

فَإِنْ أَصابَتْكُمْ مُصِيبَةٌ, a calamity (from killing or defeat), فَضْلٌ مِنَ اللَّهِ, a bounty from Allah (from conquest or spoils), لَيَقُولَنَّ, he will surely say. Al-Hasan read لَيَقُولَنَّ with a damma on the lam, returning the pronoun to the meaning of "man," because لَمَنْ لَيُبَطِّئَنَّ carries the sense of a group. The clause كَأَنْ لَمْ تَكُنْ بَيْنَكُمْ وَبَيْنَهُ مَوَدَّةٌ ("as if there had never been any affection between you and him") is a parenthetical insertion between the verb, which is لَيَقُولَنَّ, and its object, which is يا لَيْتَنِي ("O that I had been"). The meaning is: as if no affection had previously existed between him and you, because the hypocrites used to show affection and friendship to the believers outwardly, while secretly plotting harm against them. Apparently, this is sarcasm, because they were the greatest enemies of the believers and the most envious of them; how could they be described as having affection, except in an inverted way, mocking their state. It is also read فَأَفُوزَ with a damma (fa-afawz) in the nominative, coordinated with "kuntu ma'ahum" (I was with them), so that being with them is linked together, and "fawz" carries the sense of wishing, so both would be wishing together. It may also be the predicate of an omitted subject, meaning: "fa-ana afawz fi dhalika al-waqt" (so I would achieve success at that time).

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 4, verses 74–76:

*yashrūna* means *yashtarūna* (they buy) and *yabī'ūna* (they sell). Ibn Mufarrigh said:

"I sold a cloak, and I wish I had not, / after the cloak I had been a *hāmah*.
O *hāmah* that calls out an echo / between al-Mashriq and al-Yamāmah."

[[Ibn Mufarrigh's verse. He sold his slave for a cloak when he was returning from Sijistan to Basra, then regretted it and prayed against himself to be killed. It is said: *ishtarāhu* means he took it and paid its price, and *sharāhu* means he gave it and took its price. The Arabs used to claim that the bones of a slain man's skull turn into a *hāmah*, that is, an owl that screeches and cries, "Avenge me, avenge me," until his blood-price is taken. *Al-ṣadā* is the male owl. *Al-Mashriq* (on the pattern of *mu'ẓam*) and *al-Yamāmah* are two specific places with a desert between them. So his saying "I had been a *hāmah*" is a *kināyah* (metonymy) for being slain. *Yā* is for alerting or for calling. The one addressed is omitted, and *hāmah* is an explanation or an apposition for the first *hāmah*. It is differentiated from it by the addition of the descriptive phrase "that calls out an echo," that is, it screeches over its male. This is an exaggeration in allusion and refinement in expression, where he turns away from the intended meaning, as if he were speaking of a real *hāmah* screeching over its male, or rather a *hāmah* that flies and screeches with the other *hāmahs* in the deserts. After this, the speech is a *majāz* (figurative usage) for the intensity of his grief, sorrow and regret over what he did.]]

﴿Those who sell the life of this world for the Hereafter﴾ are the hypocrites, who were urged to give up the hypocrisy within them and to purify their faith in Allah and His Messenger, and to strive in the way of Allah with the striving due to Him. Those who "sell" are the believers who prefer the Hereafter over the present world and exchange the one for the other. The meaning is: if those whose hearts are diseased and whose intentions are weak hold back from fighting, then let those who are steadfast and sincere fight. The one who fights in the way of Allah, whether he is victorious or is granted victory, is promised a great reward for his striving to strengthen the religion of Allah.

﴿And the oppressed men, women and children﴾: there are two possibilities regarding *al-mustaḍʿafīn* (the oppressed). It may be in the genitive (*majrūr*) as a conjunction (*ʿaṭf*) with "the way of Allah," meaning: in the way of Allah and in the deliverance of the oppressed.

[[Mahmud said: "It is permissible that *al-mustaḍʿafīn* be in the genitive... to his saying... and in the accusative..." Ahmad said: In this reading there is an emphasis on urging their rescue from two angles. The first is specification after generalisation, for it requires the implied governing verb *ikhtaṣṣa* (he specified). Were it not for the accusative, the specification would be known from the singling out by mention. But this known matter is affirmed by way of necessary implication, by bringing it out into speech.]]

It may be in the accusative (*manṣūb*) by specification (*ikhtiṣāṣ*), meaning: "and the deliverance of the oppressed is specified from the way of Allah," because the way of Allah is general to every good, while the deliverance of the oppressed Muslims from the hands of the disbelievers is among the greatest and most specific good.

The *mustaḍʿafūn* are those who embraced Islam in Makkah, whom the polytheists prevented from migrating, so they remained among them, humiliated and oppressed, suffering severe harm from them. They used to call upon Allah for deliverance and seek His help, so Allah facilitated for some of them the departure to Madinah. Some of them remained until the conquest, until Allah made for them, from Himself, the best protector and helper, who was Muhammad (ﷺ). He took the best care of them and gave them the strongest support. When he (ﷺ) left, he appointed ʿAttāb ibn Asīd over the people of Makkah, and they saw from him the guardianship and support they wanted. Ibn ʿAbbas said: "He used to support the weak against the strong, until they were more honoured by him than the oppressors."

If you ask: why are the children mentioned? I say: it is to record the extreme extent of their oppression, since their harm reached even the children who are not legally responsible, as a humiliation to their fathers and mothers and a hatred for them because of their position. Also, the oppressed used to include their children in their supplications, to bring down Allah's mercy through the prayers of the young who had committed no sin, just as the people of Yunus did, and as the Sunnah has reported their being brought out for *istisqāʾ* (prayer for rain). It is reported from Ibn ʿAbbas: "I and my mother were among the oppressed, from the women and the children."

It is also permissible that by "the men and the women" is meant the free men and the free women, and by "the children" the male and female slaves, because a male slave is called *walīd* and a female slave *walīdah*. It was said that "the children" (*al-wildān*) and the female children (*al-walāʾid*) are referred to together as "*al-wildān*" by way of *taghlīb* (giving precedence to the masculine over the feminine), as one says "the fathers" and "the brothers."

If you ask: why is the word "oppressor" (*al-ẓālim*) mentioned when the thing it describes is feminine? I say: I came across a subtle point in this verse: every town mentioned in the Noble Book has oppression attributed to it figuratively, as in His saying ﴿And Allah strikes a parable: a town that was secure and tranquil...﴾ up to ﴿so it denied the blessings of Allah﴾, and His saying ﴿And how many a town have We destroyed, which exulted in its livelihood﴾. But this town in Surah al-Nisa is one to which oppression is attributed to its people in reality, because what is meant by it is Makkah, so the attribution of oppression to it was avoided, as an honour to it, which Allah the Exalted honoured.

I say: it is an attribute of the town, except that it is attributed to its people. So it takes the *iʿrab* (grammatical case) of "the town" because it is its attribute, and it is mentioned in the masculine because it is attributed to the people, just as you say "from this town whose people were oppressive." If it had been feminine, saying "*al-ẓālimah* ahluhā" (its oppressive people), it would have been permissible, not because the described noun is feminine, but because *ahl* (people) can be masculine or feminine.

If you ask: is it permissible to say "*min hadhihi al-qaryah al-ẓālimīn ahluhā*" (from this town whose oppressive people...)? I say: yes, as you say "*allatī ẓalamū ahluhā*" (which its people oppressed), according to the dialect of those who say *akalūnī al-barāghīth* (the fleas ate me), and from it is His saying ﴿and they secretly conferred, those who did wrong﴾.

Allah encouraged the believers with encouragement and cheered them on, by informing them that they fight only in the way of Allah. So He is their guardian and helper, while their enemies fight in the way of Satan, so they have no guardian except Satan. And the plotting of Satan against the believers, compared with the plotting of Allah against the disbelievers, is the weakest and most feeble thing.

I say: I came across a subtle point in this verse: every town mentioned in the Noble Book has oppression attributed to it figuratively, as in His saying ﴿And Allah strikes a parable: a town that was secure and tranquil...﴾ up to ﴿so it denied the blessings of Allah﴾, and His saying ﴿And how many a town have We destroyed, which exulted in its livelihood﴾. But this town in Surah al-Nisa is one to which oppression is attributed to its people in reality, because what is meant by it is Makkah, so the attribution of oppression to it was avoided, as an honour to it, which Allah the Exalted honoured.

I say: it is an attribute of the town, except that it is attributed to its people. So it takes the *iʿrab* (grammatical case) of "the town" because it is its attribute, and it is mentioned in the masculine because it is attributed to the people, just as you say "from this town whose people were oppressive." If it had been feminine, saying "*al-ẓālimah* ahluhā" (its oppressive people), it would have been permissible, not because the described noun is feminine, but because *ahl* (people) can be masculine or feminine.

If you ask: is it permissible to say "*min hadhihi al-qaryah al-ẓālimīn ahluhā*" (from this town whose oppressive people...)? I say: yes, as you say "*allatī ẓalamū ahluhā*" (which its people oppressed), according to the dialect of those who say *akalūnī al-barāghīth* (the fleas ate me), and from it is His saying ﴿and they secretly conferred, those who did wrong﴾.

Allah encouraged the believers with encouragement and cheered them on, by informing them that they fight only in the way of Allah. So He is their guardian and helper, while their enemies fight in the way of Satan, so they have no guardian except Satan. And the plotting of Satan against the believers, compared with the plotting of Allah against the disbelievers, is the weakest and most feeble thing.

(كُفُّوا أَيْدِيَكُمْ) "Restrain your hands" — i.e., refrain from fighting. The Muslims were restrained from fighting the disbelievers as long as they were in Makkah, and they used to wish that permission would be given to them for it. But when fighting was prescribed for them at Madinah, a group of them [[The phrase "كع فريق منهم" means: they were cowardly. So says al-Sihah (Sahih al-Jawhari). (ʿAyn)]] (feared), not out of doubt in the religion nor aversion to it, but out of aversion to exposing their lives [to danger] and out of fear of death, "like the fear of Allah" — with the verbal noun in the genitive construction — toward the object. If you ask: what is the grammatical position of (كَخَشْيَةِ اللَّهِ)? I say: its position is accusative as a circumstantial (ḥāl) from the pronoun in (يَخْشَوْنَ), meaning: they fear people like the people who fear Allah, i.e., resembling the people who fear Allah, "or even more intense fear" (أَوْ أَشَدَّ خَشْيَةً), meaning: or more intense fear than the people of the fear of Allah. And "more intense" is coordinated with the circumstantial. [[Maḥmūd said: "His statement, Exalted is He, (كَخَشْيَةِ اللَّهِ) is in the genitive construction of the verbal noun..." etc. Aḥmad said: A parallel to this verse has already passed in the grammatical discussion, namely His statement, Exalted is He: (فَاذْكُرُوا اللَّهَ كَذِكْرِكُمْ آباءَكُمْ أَوْ أَشَدَّ ذِكْراً). Al-Zamakhsharī had read there, and then acquiesced here, the genitive reading as coordinated with "remembrance" (al-dhikr), and we explained there its permissibility by the interpretation al-Zamakhsharī mentions here, namely attaching it to the pattern of "jadd jaduhu" (a fully-fledged, emphatic usage). The origin of this grammatical analysis is by Abū al-Fatḥ, and I have shown the permissibility of the genitive coordinated with "remembrance" without needing the mentioned interpretation, and I apply the same here, which is a good approach I deduced from the book of Sībawayh. If I am correct, it is from God, and if I am wrong, it is from me, and God is the Granter of success. What Sībawayh mentioned is the permissibility of the speaker's saying: "Zayd is the bravest of people, a man" — then Sībawayh said: "man" stands in apposition to the subject; you may also put it in the genitive and say: "Zayd is the bravest man," and this is the original form. End of the intended quote from Sībawayh. When you build on this, it is permissible to say: "So-and-so feared with a more intense fear," putting "khashya" in the accusative while meaning the verbal noun, as if you had said: "So-and-so feared a fear more intense [than] fear," so that the second "khashya" falls on the first. If you put it in the accusative, it is like what you said: "Zayd is the bravest man (ra'ulan)," where "rajulan" falls on Zayd. And if you put it in the accusative, it is on the original form: you say "ashadd khashya" and put it in the genitive, just as the original is to say "Zayd is the bravest man" and put it in the genitive. What prevented al-Zamakhsharī from the accusative, although it falls on the verbal noun, is that the implication of the accusative in such a construction is that the accusative noun departs from the first, unlike the genitive. Do you not see that you say "Zayd is more generous than a father," so Zayd is among the sons, and you are preferring his father; and you say "Zayd is more generous than a father," so he is among the fathers, and you prefer him. So if you go to make "ashadd" fall on the first "khashya" while you have made its specifier accusative, it entails that the second departs from the first, which is impossible, since fear would not be fear [in that case], requiring the mentioned interpretation, namely making the first "khashya" a fearing subject so as to remove it from the verbal noun that specifies it. We have shown in Sībawayh's discussion the permissibility of the accusative with the second falling on the first, just as with the genitive, so the same is permissible in the verse without interpretation, and God knows best. Several grammatical aspects have passed in the verse of al-Baqarah, some of which are impossible here due to conflict with the meaning, and God is the Granter of success. Such types of grammar are, in Arabic, like pure marrow, which cannot be reached except after passing through the whole of the husks, and your Lord is the Opener, the All-Knowing.]] to the object. (أَوْ أَشَدَّ خَشْيَةً) ...

The reading (yudrikkum) is with a raf' (nominative) ending. It was also said that it is on the omission of the fa' (the particle of consequence).

[Mahmud said: "It was read yudrikkum with raf'. It was also said that it is on the omission of the fa'..." Ahmad [Ibn al-Munayyir] said: As for the explanation he attaches to Sibawayh's analysis of the two verses mentioned, there is room for scrutiny. As for his statement "wa la na'ib" (nor a crier), it is the preferred view, because the insertion of the ba' (bi-) in the predicate of laysa (is not) is not a consistent or dominant rule, while the predicate is a known place for it. So when you estimate it where it is dropped, this estimate is applied to the conjoined element, for the reason we have mentioned, namely the prevalence that requires attaching its insertion to the obligatory original form, whether it is pronounced or left unstated. As for estimating (ayna ma takunu) (wherever you may be) within the meaning of another utterance, such that yudrikkum (it will overtake you) is raised by it, that is an estimate for which no parallel is known, and this estimated element has not become dominant so as to be linked with the prevalence of inserting the ba' in the predicate. Therefore, observing what the common and familiar usage requires does not oblige observing what has no precedent in usage.

As for the other verse of Zuhayr, what is transmitted from Sibawayh is that he interpreted it, or something like it, as involving inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir), like the saying:

"O Aqra' ibn Habis, O Aqra'! Indeed, if your brother is struck down, you will be struck down."

So it is not of the type of "wa la na'ib." And Allah is the Granter of success. In the last explanation that al-Zamakhshari offered there is clear proof that being killed in battles and wars does not contradict a predetermined term by any deficiency, and that every person slain has died by his term, not as the Qadariyya (the sect that denies predestination) claim. And Allah is the Granter of success.]

It is as if it was said: "Then death will overtake you." It is likened to the saying of the speaker:

"Whoever does good deeds, Allah will reward them;
The evil done by evil with Allah is two equal things.
Indeed, this worldly life and its adornment
Are like provision; there is no escaping that one day it will perish."

These verses are attributed to ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Hassan. It is also said to be by ʿAbd Allah ibn Hassan, and also said to be by Kaʿb ibn Malik al-Ansari. The meaning: whoever does good deeds, Allah will reward them, that is, will repay him for them many times over. So the fa' was dropped from the response of the conditional, which is rare. It was also said that this is specific to poetry. It is reported from al-Mubarrad that it applies generally, and he claimed that the transmitted wording is "whoever does good, al-Rahman will reward him," and "the evil [is] involved with evil or achieved by it." Then he said: "They are equal with Allah; the requital does not exceed the sin." Or the ba' means "with," that is, "evil with evil are two equal things with Allah," but the first is the sin and the second is its recompense, and it was called evil by way of mushakala (matching of expression). The reading "sayyan" (equal) is reported instead of "mithlan" (two like things), because the adornment of this world, namely wealth and children, is nothing but like the provision with which one equips himself to reach the final return; and it must perish one day, so this world must perish. So yawman (one day) is an adverbial complement of fan (perish).

It may be said: it is an attachment to what occupies the position of "ayna ma takunu" (wherever you may be), which is "ayna kuntum" (wherever you were), just as "wa la na'ib" was attached to what occupies the position of "laysu musliḥin" (they are not reformers). [His statement "as 'wa la na'ib' was attached to what occupies the position of 'laysu musliḥin'" is from the words of the poet:

"Ill-omened ones, not reformers of their tribe,
Nor a crier, except that its raven's croak is clear."

(ʿ)] And it is laysu bi-musliḥin (they are not reformers), so it was given raf' just as Zuhayr gave raf' in:

"He says, 'I have no absent property, nor is anything forbidden [to me].'"

[It is the generous man whose gift reaches you
Freely, and at times he is wronged and so wronged.

And if a needy friend comes to him in a day of hunger,
He says, "I have no absent property, nor is anything forbidden [to me]."

These lines are by Zuhayr ibn Abi Sulma, praising Hirm ibn Sinan. Al-sa'il means the gift. ʿAfwan is a circumstantial accusative: easy for him, that is, little in his estimation, even if it is much in reality, or without being asked. "Yuzlam" means he is asked beyond his capacity, so he exerts himself and gives. It is also reported as "fa-yuzlam," and its original form is yazhtalim, the reflexive of zalamahu. The ta' of the iftaʿala pattern was changed to ṭa' after an emphatic consonant, according to the original rule for the ta' of the iftiʿal pattern, then the ṭa' was changed to a ẓa' with a dot, contrary to the original rule for change in assimilation, and the first was assimilated into it. It is also reported as "fa-yaṭlam," whose original form is also yazhtalim: the ta' was changed to an unpointed ṭa', then the ẓa' was changed to an unpointed ṭa' too, according to analogy, and it was assimilated into the second. It is also reported as "fa-yuẓṭlam," with both. His statement "aḥyanan" (at times) contains a kind of precaution against the supposition that he is described as continually barren. "Wa in atahu khalil" means one who is characterized by khullah (with a fatḥa), which is poverty and destitution, which permits him to take his wealth and he does not make excuses. So his statement "yaqulu ... to the end" is a metaphor for that, and it is the response of the conditional. It is in the raf' form because the conditional is a past verb which did not affect the jussive in its form, and the present-tense response of the conditional may be in the raf' form because it is imagined to be a past verb, like the issue of coordination on the basis of supposition. It was also said that it is on the estimate of a fa', that is, "fa-huwa yaqulu" (so he says). It was also said that the estimate is: "yaqulu: la ghaʾib māli" (he says: I have no absent property), "if a friend comes to him," and the response is omitted, indicated by what has been mentioned. This is Sibawayh's view, while what precedes is the view of the Kufans, which is also reported from him. "Al-masghaba" is hunger. "Ḥarim" is like ḥadhar, a verbal noun from ḥarramahu when he prevented him, and the intended sense is the passive, that is, he is not deprived and prevented from the requesters. It is also possible that it is an adjective of the form like ḥadhar and fariḥ, in the sense of ṣaniʿ. If "ḥarim" were read with fatḥa in the sense of ḥarām, like zamin and zaman, it would be permissible, but its consequence would be that there is the fault of sinad in the rhyme.]

This is the grammatical view of Sibawayh. It is also permissible that it be connected to His statement: "and you will not be wronged the slightest bit" (wa la tuzlamuna fatilan), that is, you will not be diminished in anything of what has been written of your terms. Wherever you may be, in battlefields of war or elsewhere, then He began His statement: ﴿Death will overtake you, even if you were in towers built high.﴾ The stop on this aspect is at "wherever you may be." Al-burūj are fortresses. Mushayyadah means raised high. It was also read mushayyadah, from shadda al-qasr when he raised it or plastered it with shid, which is lime plaster. Nu'aym ibn Maysara read mushayyadin with a kasra on the ya', as a qualifier of "burūj" through the action of its doer, metaphorically, as they say: "qaṣīdah shāʿirah" (a poem that makes poetry), while the poet is its composer. Al-sayyi'ah applies to affliction and sin, and al-ḥasanah applies to blessing and obedience. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And We tested them with good things and bad things, that perhaps they would return.﴾ And He said: ﴿Indeed, good deeds remove bad deeds.﴾ The meaning: if a blessing from fertility and ease befalls them, they attribute it to Allah; and if an affliction from drought and hardship befalls them, they attribute it to you and say: "It is from you, and it was only because of your ill omen," as Allah related about the people of Moses: ﴿And if an evil befalls them, they ascribe it to bad omen from Moses and those with him.﴾ And about the people of Salih: ﴿They said, "We consider you and those with you to be an ill omen."﴾ It is reported about the Jews, may they be cursed, that they considered the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) an ill omen, and said: "Since he entered Medina, its fruits have decreased and its prices have risen." So Allah responded to them: ﴿Say, "All is from Allah."﴾ He extends provision and restricts it according to what is in the interest [of His creatures], ﴿but these people do not come close to understanding any statement,﴾ so that they would know that Allah is the Extender and the Restrainer, and all of that proceeds from wisdom and rightness. Then He said: ﴿What comes to you, O human,﴾ addressing generally, ﴿of good,﴾ that is, of blessing and benevolence, ﴿is from Allah,﴾ as a favor from Him, and kindness, and grace, and trial. ﴿And what comes to you of bad,﴾ that is, of affliction and calamity, ﴿is from yourself,﴾ because you are the cause of it by what your hands have earned: ﴿And whatever affliction strikes you is because of what your hands have earned, and He pardons much.﴾ It is reported from ʿAʾisha, may Allah be pleased with her, that no Muslim is afflicted with fatigue or hardship, even a thorn that pricks him, or the breaking of his sandal strap, except because of a sin; and Allah pardons more than that. ﴿And We have sent you to the people as a messenger,﴾ that is, a messenger to all the people; you are not a messenger to the Arabs alone, you are a messenger to the Arabs and non-Arabs, like His statement: ﴿And We have not sent you except comprehensively to mankind,﴾ and ﴿Say, "O mankind, indeed I am the messenger of Allah to you all."﴾ ﴿And sufficient is Allah as a witness﴾ to that. So it is not fitting for anyone to depart from your obedience and following.

Commentary of al-Zamakhshari (al-Kashshaf) on surah 4, verse 80:

﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger has obeyed Allah.﴾ This is because he does not command except what Allah has commanded, and he does not forbid except what Allah has forbidden. So his obedience, in carrying out what he commands and in refraining from what he forbids, is obedience to Allah.

It is related that he said: "Whoever loves me has loved Allah, and whoever obeys me has obeyed Allah" [[I have not found it.]]. Then the hypocrites said: "Do you not hear what this man says? He has committed shirk, and yet he forbids worship of anyone other than Allah! This man only wants us to take him as a lord, just as the Christians took Jesus [as a lord]." So [Allah] revealed: ﴿But whoever turns away from obedience and disregards it, [then] We have not sent you as a guardian over them.﴾ That is, you are not a watcher (ḥafīẓ) or a overseer (muhaymin) over them, watching over their deeds, calling them to account for them, and punishing them, like His saying: ﴿And you are not a guardian over them.﴾

﴿And they say, "Obedience."﴾ **Bil-raf'** (in the nominative), meaning: our affair and our matter is obedience. It may also be read in the accusative (**naṣb**), in the sense of "We obey you with obedience." This is like the speech of one who says: "Sam'an wa ṭā'atan" (We hear and we obey), and "Sam'un wa ṭā'atun." A similar usage is the statement of Sībawayh:

"We heard from some of the Arabs whom one can trust, who is asked, 'How did you wake up?' and he replies, 'Praise of God and thanks to Him' (ḥamdu Allāh wa thanā'un 'alayh). It is as if he said: 'My affair and my matter is the praise of God.' Had he put 'praise of God and thanks to Him' in the accusative, it would have been as a verb." The nominative indicates the firmness and stability of obedience.

﴿A group among them plotted by night﴾ (**bayyata ṭā'ifatun**), meaning: they devised and arranged a speech other than what you say, that is, other than what you said and commanded, or other than what they said and pledged of obedience. This is because they nullified rejection rather than acceptance, and disobedience rather than obedience. They are hypocrites in what they say and show.

**Tabyīt** (planning by night) may derive from **al-baytūtah** (spending the night), since it is the settling and arranging of a matter at night; one says, "This is a matter planned at night" (amr bayt bi-layl). Or it may derive from **abyāt al-shi'r** (verses of poetry), since the poet composes and arranges them.

﴿And God records what they plot by night﴾: He records it in the pages of their deeds and will recompense them for it, as a threat. Or He records it among what is revealed to you, so He informs you of their secrets, lest they think that their concealment will benefit them.

﴿So turn away from them﴾, and do not let your soul entertain thoughts of vengeance against them. ﴿And put your trust in God﴾ regarding their affair, for God is sufficient for you against their harm, and He will avenge you against them when the affair of Islam grows strong and its supporters are mighty.

It was recited as **bayyata ṭā'ifatun** with idgham (assimilation of the two identical letters) and the verb in the masculine form, because the feminine of **ṭā'ifah** is not real (ḥaqīqī), and because it carries the meaning of **firqah** (group) and **fawj** (band).
